So what is it about Free Speech that the new Reddit Tiananmen Square Tank captain does not seem to appreciate?

What cultural nuance are her pack of flying censorship monkeys missing?

I think it is this. Good ideas triumph over bad ideas when the arguments play out.

In China and in most of the World you don't get to play out the arguments. Good ideas and bad ideas are both quashed as the State and the State Media direct the message.

Reason takes a back seat in these cultures. Power is everything.

So how was it when the West was battling with Kings and notions of Divine Right? How far different is that supremacist notion of divine right from the arrogant idea that Reddit can do, and therefore SHOULD do, what ever it wants to do? Seems like both streams of thought flow from the same septic tank.

In the 1700s, heretical ideas, some that did not pass the test of time, were being flung about and no establishment figure in Britain would ever have taken the risk of being personally identified as being in the camp of "radicals". But the private owners (Reddit Owners?) respected the living heritage of the Enlightenment and the notion that REASON, if allowed to take the form of public debate and argument, would change the world. So they allowed arguments that they did not necessarily subscribe to to take place. There is no evidence that all these press operators held the same views but they let the dialogue take place anyways.

The free market of ideas was felt to be the highest value.

It was , indeed, the Private printing presses that allowed the radical message of conscience, autonomy, and free discussion to go forward so as to inform the Town Square of the debate and the choices that society could now make.

Imagine if it had been otherwise! Without the argument, without people's ability to weigh the conflict between great thinkers, like Hobbes vs Paine or even Jefferson vs Adams, there would never have been a Republic for this 21st century Reddit to call its home in SF, CA.

Can a Tiananmen Square Tank Driver think outside her narrow interest to the legacy they hold (or crush) in their hands?

Go out your door right now and walk to the "Public Square" in your town. Good luck finding it, right? Where the hell is that public square today? Even if you go to a pub the owner will tell you "No politics or religion can be discussed here. We are just a pub!". No public square there.

Do you recall the world as it was before the Internet? I am talking the about late 1980s and before. Where was the public square then? No where? Or was it in some tightly scripted public "debates"? Scary. This explains a lot of how low the West has fallen IMO. The lack of a public square, of the sharing of ideas is a drag if not a poison on a democracy.

But we have the internet now. And it is manifestly in the public's trust no matter what the Nabobs and Free Market zombies have to say. The FCC is the public's voice and the arm of the collective public will on this. We KNOW this. WE THE PEOPLE do own the Internet and should we decide to exert our influence, our influence will be felt.

More, WE the People control the Public square and the public square is now, for better or for worse, on the internet. Reddit is part of that public square. Or it at least was until the Tanks drove over free speech there.

When you "walk to" that public square you will find it either on the Internet or NO WHERE and if it is not on Reddit any longer, and it is not, then it is on sites like VOAT.co that declare their prime allegiance to Free Speech.

The shameful thing now is that you vested redditors are so busy arguing over how best to make absolutely sure that your own society withers and dies for the sake of Reddit doing what ever the hell it wants.

What a bunch of stooges and low born products of the modern age you folks, you mods, you Tiananmen Square Children of Tank Drivers, turned out to be.

For the rest, Go VOAT.CO young man.
